newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares end lower following Dow's fall.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares end lower following Dow's fall.

text.p: Israeli shares closed lower on Sunday in moderate trading following the decline of overseas markets on Friday, traders said.

The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares fell 1.41 percent, or 0.68 points, to 204.80 on all-share turnover of 78 million shekels against 96 million shekels on Thursday, the last day of trading before the Israeli weekend.
The Maof 25 blue chip index fell 0.68 percent to 214.94.

"The market was reacting to the decline of major world markets (following comments by U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan). Despite that the mood in the market is positive," said Michael Weiss at Evergreen Capital Markets.
"The fact that the reaction was very moderate is a very good sign. The reaction of European markets was much stronger. We are all waiting for the opening of Wall Street on Monday," Weiss added.

"We were expecting a much sharper fall following the decline of overseas markets. The main activity today was in small- and medium-capitalisation stocks as local investors are coming into the market," said Ron Weisberg at IBI Investment House.

The most active shares were Teva Pharmaceutical Industries, which fell 1.0 percent to 153,355 on turnover of 5.6 million shekels; Bank Hapoalim, which gained 0.25 percent to 508 on volume of 3.8 million shekels; and Koor Industries, which lost 1.5 percent to 27,667 on volume of 3.8 million shekels.
